drafted_from: workflow:bring-in-a-framework's row in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json (its input schema, steps and submit shapes)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:bring-in-a-framework for the book The Bakery Handbook by Sam, from the file bakery-handbook.md in my files." It reads the file whole and keeps every question and exercise as a private, source-cited framework file.
no_lists_because: It writes one private JSON framework file in the person's own files (/Frameworks/<framework id>.framework.json), not rows of a list.
instructions: 1. Put the author's own source (a book, notes or a conversation export) in your files and note its exact file name.
2. Say "Run workflow:bring-in-a-framework" with title, author and sources (the file names).

3. The AI works the steps sources, extract and verify: read the file whole, write /Frameworks/<framework id>.framework.json with every question and exercise verbatim and cited by line range, then re-read it against the source.
4. Read the verify step's counts and its missing list (empty when nothing is lost); the file stays private.
5. Say "Run workflow:work-through-a-framework" on the new framework to use it.

worked_examples.title: A two-part handbook is read into parts with line ranges
worked_examples.ask: Bring in The Bakery Handbook by Sam as a framework.
worked_examples.given: Read from the workflow row: the person gives title "The Bakery Handbook", author "Sam" and the source file bakery-handbook.md, a 96-line manuscript whose lines 1-48 are "Opening the shop" and lines 49-96 "Closing the shop". The sources step reads the whole file and records each part with its file and line range.
worked_examples.hands_back: The submit shape of step sources: {"read":["bakery-handbook.md"],"framework_title":"The Bakery Handbook","author":"Sam","parts":[{"id":"part-1","title":"Opening the shop","source":{"path":"bakery-handbook.md","lines":"1-48"}},{"id":"part-2","title":"Closing the shop","source":{"path":"bakery-handbook.md","lines":"49-96"}}]}
